svg.font-family: -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'SF Pro Text', 'Helvetica Neue', Arial, sans-serif
svg.title: Component · PicPlace status · preview-nearby · phone
svg.desc: Mirrors PicPlaceStatusCard (App/PicPlace/PicPlaceViews.swift) in its .previewOnly state when a device NEARBY holds the originals (nearby originals, docs/nearby-originals-plan.md; code 2026-09-28): the project is a preview on this device — its records and poster pulled from PicPlace — and another device of the same PicPlace account, on the same network with LetsLapse open, answered the holdings question with every original. `nearbyOffer(for:)` reads it from the holdings already known (`model.nearby.offer(for:shortfall:)`, never a folder walk in a body); the card asks for it as it appears — `.task(id: picplace.canSync)` runs refreshProject, `model.loadHoldings(for:)` and `model.nearby.want(captureID)` — and redraws when `nearby.$answers` moves, so the offer lands a beat after the screen opens and goes when the device stops answering. HEIGHT 118 pt: the template's 144 less its 26 pt note. THE GLYPH is preview-only's: statusGlyph(for: .previewOnly) answers the grey camera.fill (#AEAEB2) whatever the offer — it does not read the nearby device (the editor's preview page slashes its camera when PicPlace lacks the originals; this card does not). THE TITLE stays 'Preview only' (title(for:)). THE CAPTION, caption(for:state:) with nearbyOffer: 'The originals are on \(deviceName), nearby' + (', and on PicPlace' when PicPlace's list holds files) + ' · \(shortfall.sizeText)' — drawn in the not-on-PicPlace form, 'The originals are on iPhone 18 Pro, nearby · 20 files · 76,3 MB' (this project's numbers — the project screen's 20-photo interval; the editor page's mirror draws the 55-frame bench shoot, '55 files · 209,9 MB'). THE ACTION, actionButton: 'Import from \(deviceName)' → 'Import from iPhone 18 Pro', 12.5 pt semibold accent, ENABLED — without the offer it reads 'Download originals', or a greyed 'Preview only' when PicPlace holds nothing to download, as here; the press → `picplace.fetch(capture, shortfall:)`, which takes the device nearby first (N12). LAYOUT, from the code laid out headlessly (SwiftUI ImageRenderer on the Mac with phoneCard's own modifiers, 2026-09-28 — the method the account card's rows were checked with; it reproduces their breaks): in the header's HStack(alignment: .top, spacing 8) the label is the less flexible of the two texts, so it is offered about half of the 277 pt the glyph, the gaps and the Spacer leave, and it WRAPS — SwiftUI keeps two words on the last line: 'Import from iPhone' / '18 Pro', leading-aligned in a 121.3 pt frame; the caption keeps the 155.7 pt left over and lineLimit(2) TRUNCATES it — 'The originals are on iPhone' / '18 Pro, nearby · 20 files · 7…': the file count shows, the size is cut (the also-on-PicPlace form is cut sooner: '18 Pro, nearby, and on Pic…'). So the header keeps the template's two caption lines and its 66 pt. THE BLENDS LINE is the template's — heavyLines skips a preview's Originals line (the header's button is that line) but not its Blends one: the project's one blend is on PicPlace, 'On PicPlace · 1 blend · 410 KB' with Download (blends go up on their own, originals only when asked — which is how a project comes to be on PicPlace without them). NO NOTE: nothing was removed here (free up space checks every file with PicPlace first, so a project whose originals were removed has them there — the ', and on PicPlace' form), no Remove is offered, no push found changed files. IMPORTING: while the files come over, state(for:) answers .syncing(progress) (the `.downloading` phase), so the card takes the syncing state's layout (picplace-status.syncing.phone.svg): the amber ↓ cloud (.cloud(.downloading)), the title 'Importing from iPhone 18 Pro' (title(for:) — the `.syncing` title with progress.source), the syncing state's bar (LL.amber on LL.controlFill, 4 pt, 28 in) with 'Listing the originals…', then 'Downloading 12 of 20 files · 45,8 MB of 76,3 MB' under it (the `.downloading` caption does not name the source), and Cancel. A failed import's sentence (`model.nearby.importError`) replaces the caption until the next press. HOOKS: the nearby bench (two Simulators bound to one picplace.test account, `LL_PICPLACE_TOKENS`; the originals `LL_REGISTER`ed on one, the project a preview on the other) with `LL_DETAIL=<uuid>` on the second while the first is open; `LL_NEARBY_IMPORT=<uuid>` presses Import.
